Tosafot on Bava Batra 174b:10:1.english: "Is it that everyone who divorces," etc. - [This means:] Perhaps he will pay [the debt] without a court and without a hadarah [a vow prohibiting himself from deriving benefit from her]:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 174b:18:1.hebrew: בר מערב דכתובה - דאף על גב דאית ליה, לא משתעבד. ומילתיה דרשב"ג מיירי באבא לגבי ברא, דמשעבד נפשיה (הג"ה. ותימה למורי, אמאי לא פריך ממתניתין):
Tosafot on Bava Batra 174b:18:1.english: The son of a guarantor for a *ketubah* - For even though he [the father] has [assets], he [the son] is not bound. And the statement of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is speaking of a father with regard to a son, [in which case] he obligates himself. (Gloss: And it is puzzling to my teacher, why [the Gemara] does not raise a difficulty from the Mishnah.)

Tosafot on Bava Batra 174b:19:1.hebrew: שכיב מרע שאמר מנה לפלוני בידי כו' - קשה לר"י: הא דבעי פ' מי שמת (לעיל בבא בתרא דף קמח:): שכיב מרע שהקדיש כל נכסיו מהו? תפשוט מהכא, דאם עמד אינו חוזר! דאי חוזר, חוזר (נמי) [כמו] במתנתו, וא"כ פשיטא דנאמן, ומאי קנוניא שייך? והלא היה יכול לחזור בו מיד! ונראה לר"י דמיירי בשכיב מרע שהקדיש כשהיה בריא את נכסיו, ואמר השתא נמי: מנה לפלוני בידי — נאמן. והאי דנקט שכיב מרע, משום דדוקא השתא מהימן, כדאמרינן בפרק שום היתומים (ערכין דף כג.) ובפ' שבועת הדיינים (שבועות דף מב:), דאין אדם חוטא ולא לו; אבל בבריא ודאי חיישינן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 174b:19:1.english: A deathbed patient who said, "A maneh is owed by me to so-and-so," etc. - Rabbeinu Yitzchak (the Ri) finds this difficult: Regarding what was asked in the chapter "Mi Shemet" (above, Bava Batra 148b): A deathbed patient who consecrated all his property — what is the law? Let us resolve it from here, [by saying] that if he recovered, he cannot retract! For if he could retract, he could [also] retract [from this admission] just as [he could] with his gift, and if so, it is obvious that he is believed, and what collusion could there be? After all, he could have retracted immediately! And it appears to the Ri that [the Gemara] is speaking of a deathbed patient who consecrated his property when he was healthy, and he now says as well: "A maneh is owed by me to so-and-so" — he is believed. And the reason it mentions a deathbed patient is that specifically now he is trusted, as we say in the chapter "Shom HaYetomim" (Arakhin 23a) and in the chapter "Shevuat HaDayanim" (Shevuot 42b), that a person does not sin when it is not to his own benefit; but with a healthy person, we certainly are concerned [about collusion]:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 174b:20:1.hebrew: אדם עשוי שלא להשביע את בניו - והיינו בשלא תבעוהו ואמר מעצמו, אבל תבעוהו והודה — חייב, כדאמר לקמן בשמעתין, דטעמא דלהשביע את בניו לא שייך התם. ו"משטה אני בך" נמי לא טענינן, אף על גב דבריא אי לא טעין טענינן ליה, דאין אדם משטה בשעת מיתה, כדאמרינן בסמוך. והא דאדם עשוי כו', אמר רבי דמשמע אפי' לא טעין טענינן ליה, דאמר בזה בורר (סנהדרין דף כט: ושם): ההוא דקרו ליה קב רשו, אמר: מאן מסיק בי אלא פלניא ופלניא; תבעוהו לדינא קמיה דרב נחמן, אמר: אדם עשוי כו', משמע דרב נחמן הוה טעין ליה הכי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 174b:20:1.english: "A person is apt not to cause his sons to have to swear" - This applies when they did not claim from him and he said it on his own. But if they claimed from him and he admitted [the debt], he is liable, as [the Gemara] states below in our passage, because the reason of "to avoid making his sons swear" does not apply there. And [the claim] "I was joking with you" we also do not argue on his behalf — even though in the case of a healthy person, if he does not argue it himself we do argue it for him, since a person does not joke at the time of death, as we say shortly. And as for [the statement] "a person is apt, etc.," the Rabbi said that it implies that even if he does not argue it, we argue it for him, as it says in [the chapter] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 29b, and there): There was a certain person who was called Kav Reshu. He said, "Who has a claim against me, if not so-and-so and so-and-so?" They summoned him to judgment before Rav Nachman, who said, "A person is apt, etc." This implies that Rav Nachman argued it for him in this way.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 174b:4:1.hebrew: ואם כתב בו התקבלתי - שכתב בעל חוב כן, גובה. בשלמא לרב הונא משכחת לה בשחייב מודה, דליכא למיחש לצררי; אלא לרב פפא היכי משכחת לה? וא"ת: אי בשחייב מודה, אפי' לא כתב התקבלתי? ויש לדחות, דכי לא כתב התקבלתי, להכי לא גבי מיתומים, דחיישי' שמא לא גבה המלוה ממנו. ומשני: שאני התם, דלהכי כתב ליה התקבלתי, דליהוי כחיה אלים, וליהוי כמלוה בשטר. וכן גרס רבינו חננאל "משכחת לה בשחייב מודה", ומפרש כדפרישית, דאלים משום דהוי בשטרא. וקשיא לן, דבערכין פ' שום היתומים (ערכין דף כב: ושם) מוכח דאיירי רב הונא ורב פפא במלוה בשטר, דפריך התם: "שום היתומים ל' יום? בשלמא לרב הונא, מוקי לה בשחייב מודה; אלא לרב פפא, במאי מוקי לה?" אמר לך רב פפא: איבעית אימא בכתובת אשה, משום חינא; אבל בבעל חוב בשטר לא מצי מוקי לה. אלא מיירי ודאי אפילו בשטר. ועוד קשיא: כיון דמוקי מילתיה במלוה על פה, א"כ אפילו בני מיעבד מצוה נינהו, נמי אין לגבות מהן, דטוענין ליורש שפרע, שהאב היה נאמן לומר פרעתי; ואפילו גדולים נינהו, פטורין מהאי טעמא. ועוד, מאי משני "דלהכי כתב ליה התקבלתי דהוי כמלוה בשטר"? מה יש לו לכתיבת המלוה להועיל לערב לגבות מיתמי, מאחר שהלוה לא כתב כלום? והיה נראה לפרש דאם כתב בו התקבלתי גובה, היינו אם כתב בשטר התקבלתי מן הערב, שכך כתב הלוה גם לערב בתוך השטר, ליפות כחו לדוחקו ולפטרו לשלם חובו למלוה, אף אם לא יתבענו המלוה עדיין — גובה. בשלמא לרב הונא בריה דרב יהושע ניחא, דאיהו חייש לצררי, והכא ליכא למיחש לצררי, דכיון שכתב גם לערב התקבלתי ועשאו כמלוה לתבעו מעצמו, אין רגיל להתפיס צררי למלוה. אבל ברישא אינו גובה, משום דחייש לצררי, דלמא אתפסיה למלוה, ואע"פ שיש ערב. וזה אין לחוש בכתב לו התקבלתי, דלמא אתפסיה צררי לערב, שאין רגילות להתפיס ליה צררי, כדאמרינן לקמן דבעובד כוכבים ליכא למיחש לצררי; אלמא אין מתפיס לערב, דאם כן ניחוש שמא התפיס לערב. ואפילו למאן דפריך "אדרבה" כו', אי לאו דאתפיס צררי לערב לא הוה מקבל לערב כדפי' בקונטרס — הכא מיהא לא מתפיס, לא למלוה ולא לערב. אלא לרב פפא קשיא: הא לאו בני מיעבד מצוה נינהו? שאני התם, דלהכי כתב לו התקבלתי, שיהא לו כח לגבות מן היתומים, ושעבד נכסיו לזה, ויש לו כח לזה. מיהו קשה לר"י מן התוספתא, דקתני "ואם כתב בו בע"ח", ולשון "בו" משמע כפירוש ר"ח. ויש לפרש קצת לפירוש ר"י, כי הלוה מכל מקום כתב לו כך, אבל הבעל חוב צוה לכתוב לו, כדי שיהא הערב קבלן גמור. והא דאמר "מצוה על היתומין לפרוע חובת אביהן", פירש ר"י דהיינו במלוה על פה, ובמקום שלא נשארו קרקעות מאביהן כי אם מטלטלין, ולא כייפינן ליתמי עבור כן, אפי' היו גדולים, כדמוכח פרק מי שהיה נשוי (כתובות דף צא:) גבי קטינא דאביי, דמדקטריף בעל חוב אלמא גדולים היו. והא דפסקינן לקמן "מלוה על פה גובה מן היורשים", היינו במקרקעי, דומיא דאינו גובה מן הלקוחות:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 174b:4:1.english: "And if he wrote in it, 'I have received'" - That is, if the creditor wrote this, [the guarantor] collects. Granted, according to Rav Huna one can find [this case] where the debtor admits, for there is no need to worry about tzererei (secret payments); but according to Rav Papa, how can one find it? And if you say: [if it is] where the debtor admits, [he should collect] even if he did not write "I have received"? One can reject this: when he did not write "I have received," that is why he does not collect from the orphans, for we worry that perhaps the lender did not collect from him. And [the Gemara] answers: It is different there, for that is why he wrote him "I have received" — so that his claim would be strong, and be like a loan with a document. And so Rabbeinu Chananel reads: "one can find it where the debtor admits," and he explains as I explained, that it is strong because it is in a document. But this is difficult for us, because in Arakhin, chapter Shom HaYetomim (Arakhin 22b, there), it is proven that Rav Huna and Rav Papa are speaking of a loan with a document, as [the Gemara] asks there: "The assessment of the orphans' [property] — thirty days? Granted, according to Rav Huna, he establishes it where the debtor admits; but according to Rav Papa, in what case does he establish it?" Rav Papa could say to you: If you wish, say [it is] a woman's ketubah, because of [the court's] grace; but for a creditor holding a document, he cannot establish it [that way]. Rather, it certainly speaks even of a document. And furthermore, it is difficult: since he establishes his statement as [referring to] an oral loan, then even if [the orphans] are old enough to perform a mitzvah, one should not collect from them, for we make claims on behalf of the heir that he paid, since the father would have been believed to say "I paid"; and even if they are adults, they are exempt for this reason. And furthermore, what does [the Gemara] answer, "that is why he wrote him 'I have received,' so that it is like a loan with a document"? What can the lender's writing do to help the guarantor collect from the orphans, since the borrower wrote nothing? It would seem to explain that "if he wrote in it 'I have received,' he collects" means that if he wrote in the document "I have received" from the guarantor — meaning that the borrower also wrote this to the guarantor within the document, to strengthen his [the guarantor's] power to press him [the borrower], and to release him by paying his debt to the lender, even if the lender has not yet claimed it — [then the guarantor] collects. Granted, according to Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua it is fine, for he worries about tzererei, and here there is no need to worry about tzererei, since [the borrower] also wrote "I have received" to the guarantor and made him like a lender, so that [the guarantor] could claim from him on his own — one is not accustomed to give tzererei to the lender [in such a case]. But in the first clause [the guarantor] does not collect because [Rav Huna] worries about tzererei, lest [the borrower] gave [tzererei] to the lender, even though there is a guarantor. And in the case where he wrote him "I have received," there is no need to worry lest he gave tzererei to the guarantor, since it is not customary to give him tzererei, as we say below that regarding a gentile there is no need to worry about tzererei; evidently one does not give [tzererei] to a guarantor, for if so we should worry that perhaps he gave to the guarantor. And even according to the one who asks "on the contrary," etc. — had he not given tzererei to the guarantor, [the guarantor] would not have accepted the guarantee as I explained in the Kuntres [Rashi] — here, at least, he gave neither to the lender nor to the guarantor. But according to Rav Papa it is difficult: are they not old enough to perform a mitzvah? [Answer:] It is different there, for that is why he wrote him "I have received" — so that he would have the power to collect from the orphans, and [the borrower] bound his property to this one [the guarantor], and this one has power [over it]. However, Rabbi Yitzchak (Ri) finds it difficult from the Tosefta, which teaches "and if the creditor wrote in it," and the word "in it" implies [the matter] as in the explanation of Rabbeinu Chananel. But one can somewhat explain [the Tosefta] according to Ri's explanation: the borrower in any case wrote him this, but the creditor instructed [the borrower] to write it for him, so that the guarantor would be a complete kablan (absolute guarantor). And as for the statement "it is a mitzvah for the orphans to pay their father's debt," Ri explained that this refers to an oral loan, and to a situation where no land remained from their father, only movable property; and we do not compel the orphans for this, even if they were adults, as is proven in chapter Mi SheHayah Nasui (Ketubot 91b) regarding Ketina of Abaye, for since the creditor seized [property], evidently they were adults. And as for what we rule below, that "an oral loan is collected from the heirs," that refers to land, comparable to [a loan that] is not collected from buyers.
